name: Louisiana
tagline: From Caddo Lake oil towns to Grand Isle, by way of Cajun prairie and bayou.
intro: Louisiana's byways cross the pine hills and oil towns of the northwest, follow Cane River and the Mississippi, wander the Cajun and Creole prairies, and run down Bayou Teche and Bayou Lafourche to the Gulf marshes. This chapter follows the Louisiana Scenic Byways program, which is run by the Office of Tourism in the Department of Culture, Recreation and Tourism rather than by the highway department, with each route drawn from DOTD's own Byways map layer. Most Louisiana byways are webs of loops and spurs rather than single roads, and the program reshaped its routes around 2010, so several older byway names survive only in national databases.

members.name: San Bernardo Byway
members.blurb: Highway 46 leaves New Orleans for St. Bernard Parish and runs down to the water at Shell Beach, past the 1815 battlefield at Chalmette and the cottages of a museum village kept for the Canary Island Isleños.

members.name: Creole Nature Trail All-American Road
members.blurb: Highways 27 and 82 cross the marsh and prairie of Cameron Parish to the Gulf, past four wildlife refuges, oak-topped chenier ridges and twenty-six miles of natural beach where migrating birds stop by the million.

members.name: Cajun Corridor Byway
members.blurb: Highway 14 crosses the rice and cane country of Vermilion Parish from Gueydan to the shrimp boats at Delcambre, by way of Abbeville, where the Steen mill has boiled cane syrup since about 1910.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Myths and Legends Byway
members.blurb: Forest roads through Vernon, Beauregard and Allen parishes cross the old No Man's Land, Atakapa and Coushatta country that later sheltered outlaws, with Civil War earthworks at Burr Ferry and a Gothic jail in DeRidder.
members.note: Shown on the map as Attakapas-Coushatta Scenic Byway.

members.name: Longleaf Trail Byway
members.blurb: Seventeen miles of forest road climb through the Kisatchie National Forest among longleaf pine, sandstone outcrops and flat-topped mesas, with overlooks at Longleaf Vista onto the wilderness that locals call the Little Grand Canyon.

members.name: Flyway Byway
members.blurb: A 55-mile loop through the rice fields and crawfish ponds of Jefferson Davis Parish ties together Jennings, Welsh and Lake Arthur, with the Lacassine refuge on the way and more than 160 kinds of birds about.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Boom or Bust National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 2 runs from Caddo Lake and Oil City east to Lake Claiborne through towns that rose and fell with oil, timber and farming, past idle oilfield equipment and the old Germantown colony.
members.note: Shown on the map as Northwest Louisiana Scenic Byway.

members.name: Louisiana River Road – All-American Road
members.blurb: Louisiana's part of the Great River Road comes down the Mississippi from opposite Vicksburg, past the Frogmore cotton gins and the state capitol at Baton Rouge, to the plantation houses of the river parishes and New Orleans.
members.note: Shown on the map as Great River Road.

members.name: Historic US 80
members.blurb: Old US 80 crosses north Louisiana farm and timber country from Ruston to the Mississippi opposite Vicksburg, through Monroe, where the Biedenharn house keeps a Coca-Cola museum and the Chennault museum tells of Delta Air Lines.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Zydeco Cajun Prairie Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Three loops wander the prairie of St. Landry, Acadia and Evangeline parishes among crawfish ponds and sweet potato fields, to Fred's Lounge, where Cajun music and dancing begin on Saturday morning.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Toledo Bend Forest Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 191 follows the Louisiana shore of Toledo Bend Reservoir through pine and hardwood country to the river town of Logansport, with a state park on the bluffs known for its bass fishing and nesting bald eagles.

members.name: Cane River National Heritage Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Natchitoches the road follows Cane River, an old channel of the Red River lined with pecan orchards and cane, past the Oakland and Magnolia plantations of the national park and St. Augustine Church, built by free people of color.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Bayou Teche National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The road keeps to the banks of Bayou Teche from Morgan City up through Franklin, New Iberia and St. Martinville to Arnaudville, passing the Chitimacha reservation and museum and the Shadows-on-the-Teche house.

members.name: Southern Swamp Byway
members.blurb: Highway 22 and old US 51 skirt the Maurepas and Manchac swamps from Sorrento past Ponchatoula to LaPlace, with a raised boardwalk into the swamp at the Joyce management area and catfish at Middendorf's.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Wetlands Cultural Trail
members.blurb: Highway 1 follows Bayou Lafourche down to Port Fourchon and Grand Isle, and the roads below Houma run out to the marine station at Cocodrie, through towns where families have shrimped and trapped for centuries.

members.name: Zachary Taylor Parkway
members.blurb: Named for Zachary Taylor, whose adopted home was Baton Rouge, this 203-mile road runs west from Bogalusa through Clinton to St. Francisville, crosses the Mississippi on the Audubon Bridge and turns north through New Roads to Pineville.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Northup Trail
members.blurb: Back roads along Bayou Boeuf trace the twelve years Solomon Northup, a free New Yorker kidnapped in 1841, spent enslaved here, from the Alexandria riverfront to the Marksville courthouse where his freedom was recognized in 1853.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Louisiana Colonial Trails
members.blurb: A web of highways across central Louisiana, chiefly LA 6 and US 84 from the Texas line to the Mississippi opposite Natchez, follows the old colonial road known as El Camino Real and the Old San Antonio Road.

members.name: Tunica Trace Byway
members.blurb: Highway 66 winds about twenty miles through the wooded Tunica Hills on the line of an old Native American portage, crossing Bayou Sara on a 1940s truss bridge and ending at the gate of the state penitentiary at Angola.
